errors.description: The argument does not establish that BFS⁺ detects the triangle when exactly one triangle vertex is at level 1. The other two vertices can be discovered earlier through different level-1 vertices, so scanning the edge between them does not by itself show the triangle is detected. The sampling bound therefore relies on an unproved claim that every sampled vertex in A succeeds.
errors.evidence: The text says: “Then b and c appear on the next level (level 2) of the BFS tree. Assuming that b is discovered before c, the triangle {a, b, c} is detected while scanning the adjacency list of b.” For example, with triangle abc and extra edges sa, sp, sq, pb, qc, a BFS from s can place a,p,q at level 1, with b discovered from p and c from q at level 2. The manuscript does not specify a BFS⁺ check that detects a triangle in this situation.
